To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the N status and the N partitioning between the above-ground biomass and the grain of spring wheat was affected by the exposure to ambient air pollution, resulting in an increased protein concentration in the wheat flour, but not in the grain yield.
ambient air pollution, especially ozone and nitrogen dioxide, has a negative effect on N metabolism, N partitioning and grain quality of wheat.

(1) air pollutants have no or only minor effects on the mineral status of spring wheat; (2) the N status of wheat is significantly affected by air pollutants, leading to an increased protein content of the grain; (3) this effect is due to a reduction of N translocated to the grain, resulting in a reduced grain yield.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of air pollution on nutrient status and grain quality in relation to N metabolism and N partitioning.
the question whether air pollution can have a direct influence on the quality of agricultural products.
the question whether air pollution can affect plant metabolism and plant quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ambient levels of air pollution in 1988 had only minor effects on the P, K and S nutrition and grain quality of the spring wheat grown in OTC at the rural site Tervuren, Belgium.
the effect of air pollutants on spring wheat is mainly restricted to the N status and grain quality.

the effects of ambient levels of O3, NOx and SO2 on the mineral status, S metabolism and N metabolism of spring wheat are very complex and depend on many factors such as the stage of plant development at the time of exposure, the duration and intensity of exposure and on the plant species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ambient levels of air pollution at the rural site of Tervuren had only a limited impact on the nutrient status of wheat.
the ambient level of air pollutants at Tervuren, Belgium, did not affect the mineral status, S metabolism or grain quality of spring-wheat, except for the N status and baking quality.
the effects of air pollution on spring wheat are not only due to direct toxic effects, but are also due to indirect effects, e.g. on nutrient partitioning and N metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of air pollutants on plant growth and grain quality can be studied in a realistic way by using open top chambers.

the use of charcoal-filtered air in open-top chambers can lead to a reduction of N translocations from the aerial biomass to the grain, resulting in increased N and protein concentrations of straw and grain.
air pollutants can affect crop quality, but not necessarily yield.
